summary.text: The Köppen climate classification sorts Earth's climates into five main groups, A tropical, B arid, C temperate, D continental and E polar, with a letter for each group and subgroup.
Wladimir Köppen first published it in 1884, and because he built it on his experience as a botanist, its main groups reflect types of vegetation.
Extra letters add seasonal rainfall and heat, so Af marks a tropical rainforest and Cfb an oceanic climate with warm summers.

facts.label: Main groups
facts.value: Five: A, B, C, D and E

facts.label: Rainforest rule (Af)
facts.value: At least 60 mm of rain every month

items.prompt: A rainy city's coldest month averages 5 °C and its warmest 25 °C. Which Köppen main group does it fall in?
items.explain: Temperate climates have a coldest month between 0 °C and 18 °C and at least one month above 10 °C.

items.prompt: In a Köppen code such as Af or Cfb, what does the second letter tell you?

options.label: How far it is from the sea

items.explain: The second letter shows the seasonal precipitation type; the third shows the level of heat.

items.prompt: Two places both get less rain than Köppen's dryness threshold: one gets under half of it, the other most of it. How are they labelled?
items.explain: Below 50% of the threshold is BW, a desert; from 50% to 100% is BS, a semi-arid steppe.

items.prompt: Köppen drew the boundaries of his main climate groups using his background in which field?
items.explain: Köppen designed the system from his experience as a botanist, so his main groups classify by vegetation type.

items.prompt: Critics said one of Köppen's groups lumped too many middle-latitude climates together, prompting the 1966 Trewartha system. Which group?
items.explain: Trewartha aimed for a more refined middle latitude zone because group C was criticised as too general.

items.prompt: An oceanic climate is coded Cfb. What does the final b tell you?
items.explain: The third letter shows the level of heat, and in Cfb the ending b means warm summers.

paragraphs.heading: Climates written in letters
paragraphs.text: The Köppen climate classification sorts all of Earth's climates into five main groups. Each group is split further by its pattern of seasonal rain and temperature. The groups are A for tropical, B for arid, C for temperate, D for continental and E for polar. It is the climate scheme people use more than any other.

paragraphs.heading: Who made it
paragraphs.text: Wladimir Köppen, a German-Russian climatologist, first published the system in 1884. He changed it several times afterward, most notably in 1918 and 1936. The German climatologist Rudolf Geiger made further changes in 1954 and 1961, so it is sometimes called the Köppen–Geiger classification. Later, in 1966, the Trewartha system reworked it to give a sharper picture of the middle latitudes, answering a complaint that group C was too broad.

paragraphs.heading: Built on plants
paragraphs.text: Köppen drew on his background as a botanist, so his main groups amount to a sorting by type of vegetation. That link to plant life makes the system useful for more than naming climates. It can help describe the state of ecosystems and pick out the main kinds of vegetation within a climate. It can also help forecast how a region's plants may change in future.

paragraphs.heading: Reading a code
paragraphs.text: Every climate gets a first letter for its main group. All except the E group then get a second letter for the pattern of seasonal rain. Groups B, C and D add a third letter for heat, while E uses its second letter for temperature. So Af is a tropical rainforest climate, Cfb is an oceanic climate with warm summers, and Dwb is a partly monsoonal continental climate, also with warm summers.

paragraphs.heading: The tropical group
paragraphs.text: In a tropical climate every month averages 18 °C (64.4 °F) or more, and there is significant rain. A tropical rainforest, Af, gets at least 60 mm of rain in every single month. In a tropical monsoon climate, Am, the driest month falls below 60 mm but stays above a threshold worked out from the year's total rain. When the driest month falls below that threshold too, the climate is a savanna, written Aw or As.

paragraphs.heading: Dry and temperate groups
paragraphs.text: The dry group depends on low rainfall. A place with under half of its dryness threshold is a desert, BW; one with half to the full threshold is a steppe, BS. A third letter can show heat: h for warm low-latitude places and k for cooler middle-latitude ones. Temperate C climates have a coldest month between 0 °C (or −3 °C) and 18 °C, plus at least one month above 10 °C.
